sources.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
supports: The Magic Flute premiered on 30 September 1791 at the Freihaus-Theater auf der Wieden in Vienna.
The work belongs to the comic Singspiel repertoire popular at the time.
Mozart conducted the first performances from the keyboard; Schikaneder played Papageno and Josepha Hofer sang the Queen of the Night.
sources.limits: This biographical page supports the listed premiere and early-performance context, not broad historical claims about the work’s motifs or every later production.

sources.organization: Digital Mozart Edition / Salzburg Mozarteum Foundation
sources.title: Die Zauberflöte KV 620
supports: The edition identifies Wolfgang Amadé Mozart and calls the work a German opera in two acts, KV 620.
It credits Emanuel Schikaneder for the text.
It records the first performance in Vienna on 30 September 1791 and lists principal roles including Tamino, Pamina, Sarastro, the Queen of the Night, and Papageno.
sources.limits: This critical-edition page supports work metadata and the named role list; it is not a complete production history.

option_mapping.Giacomo Puccini: composer of Turandot; Franco Alfano completed material after Puccini’s death

sources.title: Giacomo Puccini Catalogue of the Works — Turandot notes
supports: The Turandot project was based on Carlo Gozzi’s 1762 drama; Giuseppe Adami and Renato Simoni are identified as librettists.
Franco Alfano was selected in summer 1925 to complete Turandot after Puccini’s death.
The first performance at La Scala on 25 April 1926 stopped after Liù’s death without an Alfano ending; the second and third performances used the revised Alfano ending.
sources.limits: The catalogue distinguishes multiple completion and performance states; do not reduce them to a claim that every 1926 performance used one identical Alfano ending.

sources.title: Turandot — 2025–26 season
supports: La Scala credits Giacomo Puccini for the music, Giuseppe Adami and Renato Simoni for the libretto, and Franco Alfano for completion of the third act.
The page describes Turandot as an opera in three acts and five scenes.
It dates the work’s world premiere at La Scala to 25 April 1926 and says Puccini died before completing the score.
sources.limits: This season page gives a concise historical overview. The more precise first-performance versus later-performance distinction is taken from the Puccini Catalogue notes.
